report.source_text: Post-mortem analysis confirmed these findings. Although partially necrotic, the renal mass and extensive metastases involving the retroperitoneum, thorax, and abdominal cavity were noted to have tumor cells with clear cytoplasm. The renal and lung blocks were positive for EMA and CA-IX. A cytology sample from his 4R lymph node biopsy was also reviewed at this time, from which lesional cells were positive for CA-IX and PAX8, with retained expression of FH and SDHB (Fig. 2). These results were most consistent with mccRCC with rhabdoid differentiation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: post-mortem diagnosis of metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (mccRCC)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old man presented with cough and shortness of breath, worsening despite treatment for diffuse bilateral pneumonia. Initial chest X-ray showed worsening bilateral pneumonia and pleural effusion, with a possible underlying mass. CT imaging revealed a 4.7 x 4.7 cm mass in the right kidney, along with enlarged retroperitoneal, mesenteric, infracarinal, and hilar lymph nodes, suspicious for widespread metastases. Thoracentesis fluid showed atypical epithelioid cells. A biopsy of a left retroperitoneal lymph node initially suggested epithelioid angiomyolipoma (eAML) based on immunohistochemistry. The patient clinically declined with worsening ventilation and thrombocytopenia, leading to comfort measures and death 1 month after initial cancer diagnosis. Post-mortem analysis confirmed metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (mccRCC) with rhabdoid differentiation, showing tumor cells with clear cytoplasm in the renal mass and extensive metastases in the retroperitoneum, thorax, and abdominal cavity. Renal and lung blocks were positive for EMA and CA-IX. A re-review of a cytology sample from a 4R lymph node biopsy confirmed lesional cells positive for CA-IX and PAX8, consistent with mccRCC.
